title: From universal colimits and pushout gluing to cartesian descent
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use infinity categories and coherent diagrams of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a presentable infinity category with finite limits, with presentability relative to $\mathcal U$. A morphism in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ is cartesian if its naturality square is a pullback. Suppose (i) colimits are universal: for every small diagram $D:K\to\mathcal C$ with colimit $L$ and maps $L\to B\leftarrow C$, the cocone $D(k)\times_B C\to L\times_B C$ is colimiting; and (ii) whenever $a\to b$, $a\to c$, $b\to d$, $c\to d$ is a pushout square in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal C)$ whose two arrows out of $a$ are cartesian, its two arrows into $d$ are cartesian. Let $K$ be any $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set, let $K^{\triangleright}$ be its right cone with cone vertex $\infty$, and let $\alpha:p\to q$ be a coherent natural transformation of diagrams $p,q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$. Suppose that $q$ is a colimit cocone and the naturality square of $\alpha$ at each edge of $K$ is a pullback. Then $p$ is a colimit cocone if and only if the naturality square of $\alpha$ at each edge of $K^{\triangleright}$ is a pullback. This includes $K=\varnothing$.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Theorem 6.1.3.9, implication (1) to (4), printed p. 548. Presentability supplies finite limits; they are spelled out explicitly in the statement. Read online at the source URL; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Use the coherent slice-core pullback functor $\rho:\mathcal C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}^{\mathrm{op}}$ of [lem-coef-slice-cartesian-colimit-criterion], now viewed covariantly into the opposite infinity category of spaces. The all-arrows class is replete and pullback stable. Presentability supplies all small colimits by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Let $0$ be initial. If $u:X\to0$ is any arrow, apply hypothesis (i) to the empty diagram with colimit $0$ and maps $0\xrightarrow{1}0\xleftarrow{u}X$. Its pullback colimit is $0\times_0X\simeq X$, so $X$ is initial. Thus every slice object $u$ is equivalent to $1_0$: the arrow $X\to0$ between initial objects is an equivalence. The mapping space in the slice from $u$ to $1_0$ is contractible, being the space of coherent factorizations through the identity. Since every slice object is equivalent to $1_0$, every object of the slice is terminal, so every morphism is an equivalence and this slice is its own core; by the clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] that the full subcategory of terminal objects of a quasicategory, if nonempty, is a contractible Kan complex, this core is a contractible space. Consequently $\rho(0)$ is terminal in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$, hence initial in its opposite, so $\rho$ preserves the empty coproduct.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.1.3.6 and proof of Lemma 6.1.3.7: strict initial object; core/space version of Lemma 6.1.3.5(2)

proof.text: Let $q$ be any pushout cocone on a span $q_b\leftarrow q_a\to q_c$. To verify condition (b) of [lem-coef-slice-cartesian-colimit-criterion], take any transformation $\alpha:p\to q$ with $p$ a pushout cocone and cartesian on this span. Specialize the pointwise-colimit assertion of [lem-coef-coherent-diagram-coyoneda] to the small ordinary category $I=[1]$ and $\mathcal B=\mathcal E=\mathcal C$. Its hypothesis on both categories is satisfied by presentability. The resulting pointwise colimits in $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)$ show that the four arrows $\alpha_a,\alpha_b,\alpha_c,\alpha_\infty$ form a pushout square in $\operatorname{Arr}(\mathcal C)$. Its two arrows out of $\alpha_a$ are cartesian, so hypothesis (ii) makes its two arrows into $\alpha_\infty$ cartesian. The remaining diagonal is cartesian too: the comparison for its composite is the composite of the two pullback comparisons, since $(U\times_V W)\times_W Z\simeq U\times_V Z$ by the pullback universal property. All components automatically belong to the all-arrows class. Thus condition (b) holds. Condition (a) of the cited criterion says exactly that $\rho$ preserves this pushout into $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.1.3.7: preservation of pushouts using Lemma 6.1.3.5(2) iff (3), under assumption (1) of Theorem 6.1.3.9

proof.text: Binary coproducts are pushouts over an initial object, so steps 1 and 2 show that $\rho$ preserves binary coproducts. Explicitly, mapping the pushout $B\leftarrow0\to C$ into any object $T$ gives the product $\operatorname{Map}(B,T)\times\operatorname{Map}(C,T)$, because $\operatorname{Map}(0,T)$ is contractible. The same mapping-space calculation holds for its image, since $\rho(0)$ is initial in the opposite target. This verifies preservation of the specified binary coproduct cocones.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.7: passage from pushouts and initial objects to finite coproducts (cf. HTT Corollary 4.4.2.5)
HTT proof of Lemma 6.1.3.7, printed p. 548: separate one summand, using the equivalent space-valued criterion 6.1.3.5(2) iff (3)

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-small-colimit-generation] to $\rho:\mathcal C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its source has all $\mathcal U$-small colimits by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Steps 2 and 4 prove preservation of pushouts and of all $\mathcal U$-small coproducts. The cited preservation theorem has no local-smallness requirement and does not require the target to have all colimits in advance. Therefore $\rho$ preserves every $\mathcal U$-small colimit. In particular, it takes the specified cocone $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ to a limit cone of spaces before passing to the opposite target.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.3.7: apply HTT Proposition 4.4.2.6, then Theorem 6.1.3.9

proof.text: Suppose first that $p$ is a colimit cocone. Step 5 gives condition (a) of [lem-coef-slice-cartesian-colimit-criterion] for the specified $q$ and $K$. The hypothesis on $\alpha|_K$ and the all-arrows choice of $S$ give all premises of condition (b); hence every square of $\alpha$ on $K^{\triangleright}$ is a pullback. Conversely, suppose all those squares are pullbacks. The cartesian-cone assertion of the same node identifies $\alpha$, coherently over $q$, with the pullback of its apex arrow $p(\infty)\to q(\infty)$. Apply hypothesis (i) to $D=q|_K$, $L=B=q(\infty)$ and $C=p(\infty)$. It says that the cocone with terms $q(k)\times_{q(\infty)}p(\infty)$ and apex $p(\infty)$ is colimiting. The coherent equivalence with $p$ makes $p$ colimiting, since the cocone mapping-space characterization in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] is invariant under equivalence. If $K=\varnothing$, the forward direction has no nondegenerate edge to check; in the reverse direction the same empty-diagram base change proves $p(\infty)$ initial. Thus no nonemptiness hypothesis on $K$ has been introduced.

source.place: HTT Theorem 6.1.3.9(1) implies (4); Lemma 6.1.3.5(2) implies (3), and cartesian apex pullback from Lemmas 6.1.3.2-6.1.3.3
